signals.note: Two games, two environments: Week 1 scored hostile (19.9, pressure on 29% of dropbacks, 155 yards) and Week 2 scored elite (76.6, pressure on 6%, 327 yards and four scores with Nacua out). The model takes the ceiling of this offense; I'm a step below it on purpose, for the age and the weeks the line doesn't hold. 94 is QB9 on my board, the floor I trust. The market's 124 is drafting the Week 1 version.

Fifty-three attempts for 312 and two scores Thursday night, in a game Green Bay ran nine times. The environment score (70.3, pressure on 12.5% of dropbacks in Week 2) says clean pocket and the volume says no run game at all, and both are why the market's 140th is wrong. Two things the metric hasn't priced: Jacobs on the exempt list indefinitely, and the right tackle out for the year. Model 99, me 104; with the model, a step more careful.

First in the order both weeks: 8 carries to Harvey's 3 in the opener, then 10 for 36 before he left Sunday in the third quarter with a hamstring, with Harvey already out with his own. Payton says both have a chance for the Rams; Coleman closed the game out (10 for 39 and the score). The model splits Denver three ways and gives Dobbins the worst of it. I have him 100th because when he's on the field he's first, and the High flag is why he isn't higher: the order isn't the risk, the hamstring is.

Ten carries in each game, 100 yards and a score in the first, 47 in the second, behind Swift's 18 and 16. The model gives him a third of the carries in a bad offense and gets 162nd; the market drafted a role he doesn't have (81st). Now Caleb is week to week, Bagent is in the protocol and Case Keenum is in line for Monday night, so the carries may go up while the points don't. I'm at 91 with a High flag: a guaranteed ten touches in a Ben Johnson offense is worth a flex spot, and not more.

Six carries for 10 in a game Houston trailed and threw 56 times, and the metric read that one game: 22, a specialist's score, after a 56.7 in Week 1 with every red-zone touch. I'm ranking the Week 1 role and the goal line, and the Bengals' front had something to do with Sunday. The line I'll hold myself to: if Marks out-snaps him in a game the Texans aren't chasing, he comes down and I'll say why.

Kamara came back and the passing downs left: 9 targets in Week 1, 2 in Week 2, with Kamara at 9 carries and 6 targets. That receiving work was the whole half-PPR case, and the market drafted him 32nd on the Week 1 version of it. The metric scores a specialist now (19.2, no third-down touches). I'm with the model: an RB2 in an even split until the split breaks.

The split turned: 9 carries to Allgeier's 5 after 11 to 17 in the opener, in a game Arizona ran 17 times and lost by 24. The metric scores what's still missing, third downs and the two-minute drill (both Allgeier's so far), and that's fair. I came down 12 spots for the ankle and the offense, not the player, and I'm still 37 spots above the model because the job is becoming his.

The lowest role score on the page: early downs only, and not many of them, before the toe took him out of Sunday's game (7 carries for 22; day to day). Warren has the passing downs. The market drafted a lead back at 65th; the model has him 115th and I have him 114th, and there's nothing to argue about.

The 1A in a committee on an offense that scored 3 points Sunday. The Week 2 phase data: every third-down back touch was his, and there were no red-zone touches to hand out. I'm 14 spots above the model because a back with 48% of the carries and the passing downs starts in most lineups, and starters are scarce; the market's 59th wants a lead back that isn't there. With Dowdle's toe, this week he might be one.

He cleared the protocol Monday and starts Sunday at Tampa Bay. I moved him up 11 and stopped at 117 on purpose: one quarter of football in a new offense, a concussion, and a metric reading (Wentz's 20-attempt game in the rain) that tells me nothing yet. The model has him QB5 on a full season of starter shares. I'll meet it partway once I've seen a full game; August's 91st is where I'm working back toward.

The metric and I are on the same side here, and the model is the holdout. Passing Game Health went from neutral (55.9) to elite (76.5) in one week: a pass rate 9.5% over expected, pressure on 8% of dropbacks, 47 attempts for 382 and three scores with Kelce back to 11 targets. The model's touchdown share is still 2025's. It will catch up or it won't; I'm not waiting on it.

Twelve carries each for him and Corum, two weeks running, and the model prices that split at 65th. The phase data from Monday says the split lives on first and second down: every red-zone touch and every two-minute touch went to Kyren, and he caught the touchdown. Role Clarity is on my side at 74.5. If Corum starts getting the goal-line work, I'll move him down and say so.
